title: CTIN EXUS: Automatic Cyber Threat Intelligence Knowledge Graph Construction Using Large Language Models
summary:
textual descriptions in cyber threat intelligence ( CTi ) reports , such as security articles and news , are rich
sources of knowledge about cyber threats , crucial for or-
ganizations to stay informed about the rapidly evolving
 threat landscape . 
 however , current knowledge extrac-
tion methods lack flexibility and generalizability , often re-sulting in inaccurate and incomplete knowledge extraction . to bridge the gap , we propose a novel framework , called CTINexus , leveraging optimized in-context learning (ICl ) of large language models ( llm ) for data-efficient knowledge extraction and high-quality cybersecurity knowl-
edge graph (CSKg ) construction . unlike existing methods , 
CTinexus requires neither extensive data nor parameter
tuning and can adapt to various ontologies with minimal
annotated examples . this is achieved through : ( 1 ) a care-fully designed automatic prompt construction strategy with optimal demonstration retrieval for extracting a wide range of cybersecurity entities and relations ; ( 2 ) a hierarchicalentity alignment technique that canonicalizes the extracted
knowledge and removes redundancy ; ( 3 ) an long-distance

key_findings: CTINexus enables data-efficient knowledge extraction from cyber threat intelligence reports.
The framework adapts to various ontologies with minimal annotated examples.
It employs a hierarchical entity alignment technique to reduce redundancy in extracted knowledge.
Long-distance relation prediction enhances the completeness of the constructed cybersecurity knowledge graph.
methodology: CTINexus utilizes optimized in-context learning of large language models for knowledge extraction, incorporating automatic prompt construction and hierarchical entity alignment techniques.
limitations: The framework's performance may vary with different types of cyber threat intelligence reports.
Limited evaluation on diverse datasets may affect generalizability.
Potential challenges in adapting to highly specialized ontologies.
future_work: Explore the application of CTINexus in real-time threat detection systems.
Investigate the integration of additional data sources for improved knowledge extraction.
Enhance the framework's adaptability to more complex ontologies.
